title: Settings disclosures and destructive confirmations use native elements — keyboard access and dialog focus are handled by the browser
evidence: Webui settings are native disclosures, not custom widgets: settings.html:17,35,55,64,99,120,136,148,159,172 are each `<details class="sect">` with a `<summary>` — natively focusable, Enter/Space operable, and state-exposed without any ARIA. The extension's equivalents are real buttons that keep aria-expanded honest: app.html:607,617,624,638 `<button class="link sect" aria-expanded="false">`, app.html:529 `#adv-toggle`, app.html:223-224 `#estat` with `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls="runtime-details"`; app.js:764-765, :769-770, :796-797 flip aria-expanded in lockstep with the hidden class. Destructive actions use the browser's own dialog: _storage.html:190 (restore backup), :208 (move database), review.html:55 (merge records), source.html:190 (restore default view).
proposed_fix: No action — and specifically, do not replace confirm() with a custom modal. Because there is no custom dialog anywhere in the product, the usual focus-trap / focus-restore obligation does not arise; the browser handles it. This is why the `no-focus-management` finding above is scoped to view switches and panel reveals only, not to dialogs.
risk: Swapping confirm() for a hand-rolled modal would newly introduce a focus-trap requirement that does not exist today. Treat that as a regression, not an upgrade.

title: The custom source radio-cards are built on real <input type=radio> with label/for — keyboard reachable with a visible focus ring
evidence: Each of the four source choices is a genuine radio in one named group, with the visual card as its label: app.html:334-335 `<input class="source-radio" type="radio" name="data-source" id="source-current" checked>` + `<label class="source-choice-label" for="source-current">`; same shape at :361-362 (`source-urls`), :388-389 (`source-file`), :433-434 (`source-addsite`).
